keyFindings.description: The new catch wraps the whole of restoreRole(), the listener's setRole included, and nothing retries it. restoreRole assigns heldRole only after that request succeeds (:565), reassertRole returns at once while heldRole is undefined (:587-588), and startup sets no roleTransferFrom, so a transient setRole failure costs the session its role for the life of the process. The comment the change adds says the opposite — 'which its next soft setRole off the heartbeat re-claims' — so the code states a recovery it does not perform. Before the catch this threw and the session did not start: loud rather than quiet, but not silent loss. The mechanism to retry already exists: set roleTransferFrom in the catch and the heartbeat's transferRole() (:662, :762) re-runs restoreRole on the next tick.

pruneStaleSessionRoles equates a role file's mtime with the session's last activity, but a healthy holder never rewrites it: the heartbeat's reassertRole returns without writing when the listener still names it holder (:587-595), and only restoreRole (:567) and rememberRole (:876) write. A session that has held its role for thirty days therefore has its only local recovery record deleted by the next session that starts, and loses its role on its own next resume or channel restart. Expiring an abandoned record is the point; expiring a live holder's is not. Either refresh the record when the heartbeat confirms the holder, or establish the session is gone before deleting.

MD_VIEWPORT_QUERY is (min-width: 768px) while Tailwind's md is 48rem (packages/dispatch/node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css:328, reached through @import "tailwindcss"). They agree only at a 16px root font size; with a 20px browser default the md: classes switch at 960px and the query at 768px, so between them the row takes the shortened directory in the layout meant to keep the whole path — the divergence the constant's own doc comment promises cannot happen. (min-width: 48rem) makes the promise true.
